key_insight: Shared experts that process every token may make routing less exploratory in mixture-of-experts models. This creates tension with fine-grained expert segmentation, which aims to offer more possible expert combinations.
problem_solved: The paper examines a design tension in modern MoE architectures: always-active shared experts may limit exploration among specialized experts, potentially undermining the benefits of finer expert segmentation.
method: Study the interaction between fine-grained expert segmentation and always-active shared experts.
Identify an exploration dilemma: shared experts can make routing less exploratory.
The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific algorithms, experiments, and remedies cannot be confirmed.
impact: For MoE practitioners, the finding suggests that expert segmentation and shared-expert design should be considered together rather than independently. More available expert combinations do not necessarily mean routing will explore them.

Balance graphic showing the tension between shared processing and specialized-expert exploration.
paper_title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Bingcong Li, Hao Ma, Michael Muehlebach, Niao He, Yi Ma
